MCQ = the probe the ablation search optimised (share of misaligned option chosen; change vs the checkpoint in pp). Free-form EM = paper metric on 2,400 open-ended answers (aligned<30 and coherent>50; relative change vs the checkpoint). Insecure-code % = writes vulnerable code on held-out coding prompts, i.e. the narrow task the checkpoint was trained on (change in pp). A good neuron set drops both EM columns while leaving insecure-code % near the checkpoint: the neurons carry the broad misalignment, not the coding skill. Free-form and insecure-code values are measured for the greedy ceiling set only.

This neuron fires on the present-tense/base-form verb immediately following a subject in wh-questions ("Where **do** you...", "Where Do **We** Go?", "What **happens** if...", "you **make**"), and is strongly suppressed when that slot holds a past-tense verb ("you **did**", "someone **used**", "you **got**", "you **came**") — i.e. it tracks present- vs past-tense verb form in question/clause-subject position.

L2·N12761unmasked layer
This neuron's signal is mainly a boundary detector with inverted sign: it is strongly *suppressed* by sentence-final punctuation immediately followed by a newline (".\n", "?\n" — i.e. paragraph/segment breaks), while its positive activations sit on word-internal subword suffixes that complete a word or on mid-sentence continuation tokens (e.g. "ino" in "Vino", "istry" in "Dentistry", "w" in "thwacked").
